name: Weight Loss
tagline: 60 days to rewire cravings and build a lean routine.
description: A neuroscience-based 60-day fat-loss program — break the sugar/craving loop, retrain hunger and reward signals, move daily, and build eating habits that stick long after day 60.

phases.label: P1
phases.title: Breaking the Cycle
phases.vibe: The first two weeks reset your palate and your habits. Cut the liquid sugar, front-load protein, and walk daily. You're weakening the cue→snack→dopamine loop that drives overeating, and teaching your body real hunger again.

phases.label: P2
phases.title: Rewiring the Brain
phases.vibe: Cravings still fire at the old times — replace the routine, not the willpower. Swap the evening snack for a ritual, train a little harder, and let a mild consistent deficit do the work. New habits are becoming automatic.

phases.label: P3
phases.title: Building a New Identity
phases.tag: A lean routine you actually keep.
phases.vibe: You now eat and move like a lean person by default. The scale is a lagging indicator of habits already locked in. You plan for the maintenance life ahead.

0.title: Water first + weigh-in
0.note: 500ml water on waking, then weigh yourself. Morning hydration curbs false hunger; a daily data point keeps you honest without obsessing.

0.title: Protein-forward breakfast
0.note: 30g+ protein (eggs, Greek yogurt, shake). Protein blunts the hunger hormone ghrelin and stabilizes blood sugar so cravings never spike.

0.title: Log everything you eat
0.note: Track every bite in an app. Awareness alone cuts intake — you can't rewire a loop you can't see.

0.title: 8,000+ steps
0.note: Walk after meals when you can. Steady low-intensity movement burns fat and blunts post-meal glucose without spiking appetite.

0.title: HALT before snacking
0.note: Hungry, Angry, Lonely, Tired? Emotional eating is a routine triggered by feelings, not fuel. Meet the real need first.

0.title: Beat one craving
0.note: Sparkling water + brush teeth, or 15 squats. Cravings pass in ~10 min; a competing action rides out the wave.

0.title: Evening journal — wins + triggers
0.note: Note what you ate well and what tripped you. Reflection turns slips into data instead of shame.

0.title: Sleep 7-9 hrs
0.note: Poor sleep raises ghrelin and lowers leptin — you literally get hungrier. Sleep is a fat-loss tool.

1.title: Water first + weigh-in
1.note: Keep the morning data habit. Trends over days matter, not any single number.

1.title: Protein + fiber breakfast
1.note: Add vegetables/fruit for fiber. Fiber slows digestion and feeds satiety — you eat less without trying.

1.title: Strength training 30 min
1.note: Lift 3-4x/week. Muscle raises your resting burn and protects your metabolism in a deficit.

1.title: Swap the evening snack ritual
1.note: Replace mindless snacking with tea + a walk or a hobby. Same cue and time, healthier routine — that's the rewire.

1.title: 9,000+ steps
1.note: Nudge the daily target up. Small increases compound over 60 days.

1.title: Plan tomorrow's meals
1.note: Decide meals in advance. Pre-commitment beats in-the-moment willpower every time.

1.title: Gratitude + reflect
1.note: Note progress you feel, not just the scale — energy, clothes, mood. Non-scale wins sustain motivation.

2.title: Morning ritual + weigh-in
2.note: Water, weigh, plan — automatic now. Systems, not motivation, carry you.

2.title: Dialed-in breakfast
2.note: Your go-to high-protein meal. Consistency at breakfast anchors the whole day.

2.title: Train — your standard now
2.note: Strength + steps are just who you are. Keep progressive overload going.

2.title: One mindful meal
2.note: Eat slowly, no screens, notice fullness. Mindful eating retrains satiety signals for the long run.

2.title: 10,000 steps
2.note: Your baseline activity. Movement is a lifestyle now, not a diet phase.

2.title: Sketch your maintenance plan
2.note: Plan how you'll eat after day 60. Weight kept off is a habit kept up.

2.title: Identity journal
2.note: Write as a lean, active person. Self-image drives behavior more than any diet rule.

quotes: You don't need more willpower — you need fewer cravings, and those you can rewire.
Every meal is a vote for the body you're becoming.
The scale is a lagging indicator of habits you already own.
Hunger is a wave, not an emergency.
Protein and steps beat motivation every time.
You're not on a diet. You're building a default.
Sleep is the fat-loss tool no one is selling you.
Discipline at the store is easier than willpower in the kitchen.
Small deficit, big consistency, real results.
Sixty days of habits outlast any 3-day crash diet.
